_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: Where the Light Gets In
suggestions.reason: A Victorian coffee warehouse loft on Rostron Brow, Sam Buckley's tasting menu the reason Stockport now carries a Michelin Green Star of its own — locally sourced, seasonal, and cooked in full view of the room.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via wtlgi.co (official site), Michelin Guide's own listing (guide.michelin.com — a Michelin Green Star specifically, not a standard star, copy reflects this precisely), Great British Chefs and Tripadvisor. 7 Rostron Brow, Stockport SK1 1JY — single site, chef-owner Sam Buckley, no other locations found anywhere. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly: independent, single-site, no chain footprint. Coordinates geocoded from the postcode (doogal.co.uk), within Stockport (Underbanks)'s existing sanity box. Reuses the existing TASTING MENU type (LI~LY precedent). High confidence — well-documented, actively trading Wed-Sat per its own current site.

suggestions.name: Bruk
suggestions.reason: A small self-funded room on Little Underbank, poured by people who left the big groups to do it properly — the list turns over by the bottle, not the season.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA's own listing, whatpub.com, manchestersfinest.com and the Food Standards Agency's ratings register (confirms current trading). 8 Little Underbank, Stockport SK1 1JT — described consistently as a self-funded independent wine bar & restaurant, single site, no other locations found. Passes Hard rule 1. Coordinates geocoded from the postcode. Reuses the existing WINE BAR type. Moderate-high confidence.

suggestions.name: Stockport Market Hall
suggestions.reason: A Victorian glass-roofed hall on Market Place trading since the 1860s, thirty-odd independent stalls under one roof — turn up for a Foodie Friday and you won't leave with the plan you arrived with.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Stockport Council's own site (stockport.gov.uk/stockport-market), thestockportmarket.co.uk and visitmanchester.com. Market Hall, Market Place, Stockport SK1 1ES — council-run Victorian market hall (1860s), not a chain by definition, same precedent as Mackie Mayor/Altrincham Market already in venues.json. Coordinates geocoded from the postcode. Reuses the existing MARKET HALL type. High confidence.

suggestions.name: FOLK
suggestions.reason: Four friends' own room on Burton Road, brunch plates giving way to small plates by evening — the covered terrace fills first, same as it's always done.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via folkdidsbury.co.uk (official site, naming co-owners Rachel Caulfield and Andy Jane), CAMRA/whatpub.com and creativetourist.com. 169-171 Burton Road, Didsbury M20 2LN — independent, single-site neighbourhood bar & kitchen, no other locations found under this name. Passes Hard rule 1. Coordinates geocoded from the postcode. Reuses the existing GASTROPUB type (Wilmslow Tavern/Charlie Brown's Hale/The Mucky Pup precedent). Moderate-high confidence — well-established, actively trading per its own current menu/events page. Named directly in this district's own editorialDescription ('FOLK on Burton Road') but never previously seeded as a venue.

suggestions.name: Marie Louise Gardens
suggestions.reason: Four and three-quarter acres off Palatine Road, gifted to the city in 1903 and kept up since by the people who live around it — paved paths and flowering trees, a Green Flag on the gate and no rush to leave.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Manchester City Council's own directory listing, didsburycivicsociety.org and marielouisegardens.org.uk (the volunteer Friends group's own site, confirming an active, maintained public park, Green Flag 2014). Palatine Road/Dene Road, Didsbury M20 2FE — a council-owned public park, not a business, so no chain concern. Coordinates cross-checked against the M20 2FE postcode area and a second independent source. Reuses the existing TOWN PARK type (Thorn Grove Park/Bruntwood Park precedent). High confidence.

suggestions.name: Chorlton Bookshop
suggestions.reason: Family-run on Wilbraham Road since 1983, a local-authors shelf that actually means something and staff who'll find the thing you half-remember the plot of.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via chorltonbookshop.co.uk (official site), manchestercityofliterature.com and creativetourist.com — family-run independent bookshop trading since 1983, single site at 506 Wilbraham Road, Chorlton-cum-Hardy M21 9AW. Passes Hard rule 1 (independent, no other branches found). Coordinates geocoded from the postcode. Introduces a new type, BOOKSHOP — no existing type fits precisely (RARE BOOKSHOP, used for Manchester Rare Books in Alderley Edge, specifically implies antiquarian/secondhand rare stock, which this general independent new-book shop isn't); left category-only (Do), same precedent as CANTONESE ROAST/FARM EXPERIENCE elsewhere in venues.json, since no onboarding tile fits a general bookshop precisely. High confidence.

suggestions.name: Chorlton Water Park
suggestions.reason: A hundred and seventy acres of lake, woodland and meadow ten minutes past the tram stop — the walk Chorlton takes when Beech Road's got too loud.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via Manchester City Council's own directory listing, cross-checked with mdoc.org.uk (Manchester & District Orienteering Club's own map of the park) and Google Maps' listed coordinates for the venue itself. Maitland Avenue, Chorlton Park, Manchester M21 7WH — a council-owned public park with a fishing lake, not a business, so no chain concern. Coordinates cross-checked against two independent sources landing within ~30m of each other. Reuses the existing RIVERSIDE PARK type (The Carrs, Wilmslow, precedent). High confidence.

suggestions.name: Giovanni's
suggestions.reason: The old Post Office at the Tatton Park end of King Street, no group behind it — proper homemade Italian and a Sunday lunch that still runs to a queue.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via the restaurant's own site (giovannis-knutsford.co.uk), Knutsford Town Council's own news items (naming it among the town's independent traders) and OpenTable/Tripadvisor listings, both showing current, active trading with recent 2026 reviews. 125A King Street, Knutsford WA16 6EH, in a Grade II-listed former Post Office building. Described consistently as Knutsford's only genuinely independent Italian restaurant — single site, no other locations found under this name (distinct from unrelated chains also present on King Street, like Gusto/Mowgli, which are correctly excluded). Passes Hard rule 1. Coordinates geocoded from the postcode. Reuses the existing ITALIAN RESTAURANT type. Moderate-high confidence.

suggestions.name: Corks Out
suggestions.reason: A wine specialist and off-licence on London Road with one sister room out in Stockton Heath — tastings most weeks, and a list built by people who'd rather talk you out of the safe bottle.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via corksout.com (official site, listing exactly two locations: Alderley Edge and Stockton Heath, Warrington), CAMRA/whatpub.com and Companies House (Corks Out (Alderley Edge) Ltd, a distinct registered entity). 73 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY. Two-site sibling footprint — same precedent already established in venues.json for Craig's/Ivy Spinningfields/Cibo-Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow, not a chain. Coordinates geocoded from the postcode (shares SK9 7DY with Fire Station Social Cucina already in venues.json — a genuine same-postcode London Road neighbour, not a shortcut). Reuses the existing WINE BAR type. High confidence.

suggestions.name: The Seven Oaks
suggestions.reason: A white faience freehouse on the Art Gallery corner of Chinatown, still pulling proper cask after the louder rooms have called last orders — real ale, real cider, and pie and mash that doesn't apologise for being unfashionable.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via CAMRA's own listing (noting its locally-listed white faience exterior), whatpub.com, the pub's own site (sevenoaks.pub) and themanc.com's feature on it. 5 Nicholas Street, Chinatown, Manchester M1 4HL — a freehouse (not tied to any brewery), single site, no other locations found. Passes Hard rule 1 cleanly. Coordinates geocoded from the postcode, within Chinatown's own district boundary (Moseley/Charlotte/Princess/Portland Street block). Reuses the existing ALE HOUSE type mapping (left in place, ready for a future venue, after The Old Dancer's removal — see venues.json's own closure note) rather than introducing a new one. High confidence.
